args.doc: Rays in one shot. Default 1. A shotgun is 7.
args.name: count

args.doc: Degrees of random cone, rolled PER RAY. Without it all seven of a shotgun's pellets travel the identical line and a shotgun is a pistol that hits seven times as hard at any range whatever.
args.name: spread

args.doc: Tracer style to draw, or absent for none -- which is what makes a hitscan a punch. Doom's own fist is a line attack with a short range, so a melee weapon and a rifle share every line of the code that fires them.
args.name: tracer

args.doc: World units per second, away from the muzzle. PER RAY, so a seven-pellet shotgun at point blank shoves seven times -- which is what a shotgun at point blank should do.
args.name: knockback

args.doc: The vertical part of that shove.
args.name: lift

args.doc: Multiplier on the target's move_speed. Needs `slow_ticks`.
args.name: slow

args.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
args.name: hit_vfx

args.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
args.name: hit_vfx_radius

actions.doc: An instant shot. The engine answers where the ray ended and what was there; what that COSTS is this action.
actions.name: hitscan

args.doc: Degrees between shots when `count` > 1.
args.name: arc

args.doc: How far in front of the body it appears, so a rocket does not spawn inside its owner.
args.name: offset

args.doc: Degrees off the aim, for a weapon that throws sideways.
args.name: angle

actions.doc: A projectile, through the mob runtime's own launcher. The owner is the PLAYER and the heading is their facing, which is why this goes through mobs.launch_from rather than the launcher a monster uses: a mob's `aim` is a steering field a player does not have.
actions.name: launch

args.doc: How far IN FRONT of the body the circle is centred. Absent or zero is centred on the player, which is a ground slam; a few units is a shockwave thrown forward. This is the "chosen point", and it is relative because a weapon does not know where it will be fired from.
args.name: offset

args.doc: And how far above the feet, for a blast that goes off at chest height rather than on the floor.
args.name: height

args.doc: Damage linear in distance rather than flat to the edge. Linear in distance and not in its square: full strength until the last inch and then nothing reads as a bug.
args.name: falloff

args.doc: Default true. False is what stops a rocket jump killing you.
args.name: hurts_owner

args.doc: Outward from the CENTRE, not from the player -- so a blast thrown forward scatters things away from where it landed.
args.name: knockback

args.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
args.name: hit_vfx

args.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
args.name: hit_vfx_radius

actions.doc: A circle of damage around a chosen point. Everything in range is hit once, walls are NOT consulted -- this is a shockwave, not a ray -- and it is the mob runtime's own blast, the one rockets have used since the cyberdemon.
actions.name: damage_area

args.doc: Which warning to draw, by catalogue id. What it LOOKS like is the catalogue's business, exactly as a tracer style is.
args.name: effect

args.doc: How big the warned area is.
args.name: radius

args.doc: How long until the blow actually lands. The number a player needs to decide whether to move.
args.name: ticks

args.doc: How far in front of the body it is centred, matching `damage_area`'s so a warning and its blast agree.
args.name: offset

actions.doc:
ANNOUNCE AN INCOMING ATTACK, so a client can draw the warning before it lands. Put one at `at = 0` of a wind-up phase and the blow itself later in the same phase; the gap between them IS the time the player has.
It carries no wire format of its own: it rides the vfx event, with the radius in 1/256 units in the low sixteen bits of `param` and the ticks remaining in the high sixteen.
actions.name: telegraph

actions.doc: Debit the pool. Default is the weapon's own `per` from its own `ammo`. AN ACTION RATHER THAN AUTOMATIC, because a charged shot costs more than a tapped one and a phase that fires twice pays twice -- neither of which a field on the weapon can say.
actions.name: consume

args.doc: Degrees of random slop on the direction.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc: A shove, in world units per second. RECOIL is `towards = "away"`; with a `vertical` it is a rocket jump. NOT PREDICTED -- the client learns about it from the next snapshot and reconciles, which is already classified as SNAP_LUA_APPLIED rather than as a fault. Making it predictable would mean the engine learning what a weapon is.
actions.name: impulse

actions.doc: For a combo step or a refire count.
actions.name: add_var

actions.doc: Enter another phase immediately. The REST OF THE SEQUENCE IS ABANDONED, which is the point: it is how a shot that finds no ammunition stops before it draws a tracer.
actions.name: goto

actions.doc: Change the animation state part way through a phase, for a phase whose `anim` covers only its beginning.
actions.name: set_anim

actions.doc: If the weapon can no longer fire, select the best one that can. Doom does this and it is not a nicety: a player who empties a shotgun while something is chasing them is otherwise holding an inert object, pressing fire and getting nothing, with fifty bullets in their pocket.
actions.name: switch_if_empty

args.doc:
Send the player's ENTITY INDEX instead of the length, which an `attach` particle kind reads as "follow this body". That is what makes a continuous spray stay on the weapon: without it each burst spawns where the event said and a moving player runs out from under it, leaving the sparks behind in a line.
There is no stop event and none is needed -- a phase that repeats pushes the emitter's deadline out, and letting go of the trigger lets it lapse.
args.name: attach

actions.doc: A visual effect at the player, by catalogue id. A muzzle flash, or with `attach` a spray that follows them.
actions.name: vfx

actions.doc: The escape hatch, called with (entity, weapon_name, phase_name).
actions.name: lua

ammo_fields.doc: What the panel calls this pool. Defaults to its own name.
ammo_fields.name: label

ammo_fields.doc: The most a player may hold.
ammo_fields.name: max

ammo_fields.doc: Where it sits in the panel. The read-out list is GENERATED from this, which is the thing that stops a new pool being invisible.
ammo_fields.name: order

conditions.doc: Fires as soon as it is reached. For the last entry in a list, and for a phase whose `ticks` are the only gate.
conditions.name: always

conditions.doc: The button went down THIS TICK. Edge-triggered, so holding it is one shot and not sixty a second. Default `primary`.
conditions.name: button_pressed

conditions.doc: The button came up this tick. What ends a charge.
conditions.name: button_released

conditions.doc: The button is down, edge or not. THIS IS WHAT AUTOMATIC FIRE IS: a chaingun's `ready` transitions on held where a pistol's transitions on pressed, and there is no `auto` flag anywhere.
conditions.name: button_held

conditions.doc: The button has been down for at least this many consecutive ticks. A charge threshold. Several of these in descending order are charge LEVELS, which is why this is a condition rather than a field on a phase.
conditions.name: held_for

conditions.doc: The weapon's own pool holds at least `n`, default its `per`. A weapon with no `ammo` always has it.
conditions.name: has_ammo

conditions.doc: The complement, stated rather than negated, so a phase graph reads as a graph. This is what routes an empty weapon to a dry click instead of a shot.
conditions.name: no_ammo

conditions.doc: This phase has been running at least this long. For a transition part way through a phase that has other business afterwards.
conditions.name: phase_elapsed

conditions.doc: 0-100, from the seeded generator, so it is reproducible with the rest of the tick.
conditions.name: chance

conditions.doc: A per-weapon counter reached a number. A combo step, an overheat.
conditions.name: var_at_least

conditions.doc: Exactly equal, for a counter used as a state rather than a level.
conditions.name: var_is

conditions.doc: Whether the body is standing on something. `value = false` is AIRBORNE, and that is what a down-slash is written with: put the airborne branch above the grounded one in `ready` and the same button does two different things. Default true.
conditions.name: grounded

conditions.doc: Moving horizontally faster than `speed` (default a half unit a second). A running attack that differs from a standing one.
conditions.name: moving

conditions.doc: Descending faster than `speed`. A stomp is this plus a press, and it is deliberately not the same as `grounded = false`: the top of a jump is airborne and is not a dive.
conditions.name: falling

conditions.doc: The escape hatch: the name of a global function, called with (entity, weapon_name, phase_name), truthy to fire. Meant to be used -- a vocabulary that covers everything is a programming language -- but everything expressible above should be.
conditions.name: lua

health_fields.doc: The ceiling a `bonus_max` pickup may trickle up to. 200 in Doom.
health_fields.name: bonus_max

phase_fields.doc: The animation state the player is put into for this phase -- the `state <n>` on a sprite line in assets/props.txt, and the same number client/src/render/animstate.js resolves. The server declares it and the client owns the timing (design §4), so this is a number, not a frame list.
phase_fields.name: anim

phase_fields.doc: How long the phase lasts. ABSENT MEANS IT WAITS -- the phase stays until a transition fires, which is exactly what a charge is. Present, it also defines a WINDOW: a transition on this phase can only fire while it is still running.
phase_fields.name: ticks

phase_fields.doc: Where to go when `ticks` run out and no transition matched. Absent returns to the weapon's `initial`.
phase_fields.name: next

phase_fields.doc: What this phase does, as an ordered list of {at = <ticks after entry>, action = ...}. `at` is a DEADLINE from entry, not a delay from the previous entry: entries fire on the first tick the phase has been running at least that long, so a dropped tick delays an entry rather than losing it.
phase_fields.name: sequence

phase_fields.doc:
A swing shape for THIS PHASE, replacing the weapon's while it is in it. Same fields as the weapon's `swing`.
THIS IS WHAT MAKES A COMBO A COMBO. Three presses reaching `hit1`, `hit2`, `hit3` was already the shape the phase graph gave -- and all three swung the identical volume for the identical damage, because `swing` was a property of the weapon and there was one of it. A finisher that hits harder and sweeps wider is the whole reason anyone writes a combo.
A phase without one leaves the weapon's in place.
phase_fields.name: swing

phase_fields.doc:
A list of {when = <condition>, to = <phase>, ...args}, checked IN ORDER every tick, first match wins. Order is the whole mechanism for a charge: put `held_for 60 -> fire_big` above `button_released -> fire` and a long hold takes the first.
`when` is a condition NAME, whose arguments sit on the transition itself, OR a list of {cond = <name>, ...args} ALL of which must hold -- the mob vocabulary's shape. The list is what lets a transition say 'the button went down AND there is no ammunition', which one condition cannot: `no_ammo` on its own fires while a weapon is merely being HELD, so an empty weapon would be taken out of the player's hands the instant they chose it, every tick, and could never be carried at all.
phase_fields.name: transitions

pickup_fields.doc: Grants this weapon, once, and selects it. Its ammunition is granted EVERY time, which is why a second shotgun on a map is still worth walking over.
pickup_fields.name: weapon

pickup_fields.doc: Grants ammunition, as {kind = n}, capped at each pool's `max`.
pickup_fields.name: ammo

pickup_fields.doc: Which health ceiling this pickup may fill to. A health bonus trickles past the normal one, which is why this is a named ceiling rather than a comparison against the pickup's own name buried in the runtime.
pickup_fields.name: ceiling

pickup_fields.doc: Sets armour to this if it is higher. Doom's green and blue.
pickup_fields.name: armour

pickup_fields.doc: This pickup is declared and does nothing, and says so when walked over, naming itself. A pickup that silently does nothing is indistinguishable from a bug -- which is the whole reason this field exists rather than the entry simply being absent.
pickup_fields.name: not_yet

swing_fields.doc: What a connected swing costs the thing it hit. SCRIPT, not a parameter: putting damage in the replicated table would hand the client the numbers to compute it with (docs/ENGINE.md).
swing_fields.name: damage

swing_fields.doc: To the target's SURFACE, not its centre.
swing_fields.name: reach

swing_fields.doc: How wide, either side of the aim. 0.125 is 45 degrees each way.
swing_fields.name: half_arc

swing_fields.doc: Where the collider starts, relative to the aim.
swing_fields.name: sweep_from

swing_fields.doc: And where it ends. Equal values make a THRUST that does not rotate at all; the default sweeps right to left through the front, which is what a swing looks like.
swing_fields.name: sweep_to

swing_fields.doc: The INNER edge, as a distance from the body's surface. Zero is a wedge starting at the body -- a fist. Non-zero makes a ring segment that misses anything pressed right up against you, which is a spear: getting inside its reach is how you beat it.
swing_fields.name: min_reach

swing_fields.doc: How long the collider is live. This is why a swing is a VOLUME MOVING THROUGH TIME rather than an instant: a target that steps out of the way mid-swing is missed.
swing_fields.name: ticks

swing_fields.doc: Where the collider starts VERTICALLY, as a turn fraction: 0 is level, 0.25 is straight up, -0.25 straight down.
swing_fields.name: pitch_from

swing_fields.doc: And where it ends. An overhead chop runs from above to level; a spear thrust upward runs the other way. Equal values are a fixed elevation, which is what a horizontal slash at chest height is.
swing_fields.name: pitch_to

swing_fields.doc: How tall the arc is, either side of the pitch. ABSENT OR ZERO MEANS NO VERTICAL CHECK AT ALL -- the swing is bounded only by the body's height, which is how every swing behaved before pitch existed and is right for a fist. Set it and an overhead swing genuinely misses something at your feet.
swing_fields.name: half_pitch

swing_fields.doc: How hard a connected swing throws the target, in world units per second, directly away from the swinger.
swing_fields.name: knockback

swing_fields.doc: The vertical part of that shove. An uppercut that pops a target into the air is this and nothing else.
swing_fields.name: lift

swing_fields.doc: Multiplier on the target's move_speed while it lasts. 0.5 is half pace; needs `slow_ticks` beside it or nothing happens.
swing_fields.name: slow

swing_fields.doc: How long the slow lasts. Tagged by the attacker, so hitting the same target twice REPLACES rather than stacking to a standstill.
swing_fields.name: slow_ticks

swing_fields.doc: A particle kind to burst where this lands, by catalogue id. Drawn entirely by the client -- nothing about it crosses the wire or enters a hash.
swing_fields.name: hit_vfx

swing_fields.doc: How wide a volume the burst comes out of. A blast wants its own radius here so the particles fill it rather than all starting at one point.
swing_fields.name: hit_vfx_radius

swing_fields.doc: Ticks before another swing may START. Capped at 255 by the parameter's width.
swing_fields.name: cooldown

weapon_fields.doc: What the weapon panel calls it. The only string a player sees.
weapon_fields.name: label

weapon_fields.doc: Selection priority, low to high. It is what the panel sorts by AND what the empty-weapon fallback picks the highest of, so running a shotgun dry drops to the pistol rather than the fists.
weapon_fields.name: order

weapon_fields.doc: Which pool this eats. Absent means it never runs out, which is what a fist and a chainsaw are.
weapon_fields.name: ammo

weapon_fields.doc: What one shot costs, debited by the `consume` action. Default 1. A charged shot that costs more says so on its own `consume`.
weapon_fields.name: per

weapon_fields.doc: Which phase the weapon rests in. Defaults to the first phase in declaration order, and the runtime returns here whenever a phase runs out with no `next`.
weapon_fields.name: initial

weapon_fields.doc: The swept melee collider, whose shape is written into the REPLICATED parameter table when this weapon is selected. Absent means this weapon does not swing -- and that is enforced through the parameter `attack_enabled`, so the client predicts the absence rather than predicting a swing the server then denies. See swing_fields.
weapon_fields.name: swing

weapon_fields.doc: How many directions aim snaps to while this is held. 0 or absent is free aim; 8 is eight-way. A replicated parameter, so the snap is predicted -- which matters, because an aim the client and the server round differently is a mispredict on every tick the stick is near a boundary.
weapon_fields.name: aim_snap

weapon_fields.doc: Per-weapon counters, by name, with their starting values. Each player gets their own copy. A refire count, a combo step, a heat level.
weapon_fields.name: vars

weapon_fields.doc: Ammunition its own pickup comes with, as {kind = n}. Doom's shotgun arrives with eight shells.
weapon_fields.name: gives
